newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya, U.N. sign petrochemical sector study deal.
newsitem.headline: Libya, U.N. sign petrochemical sector study deal.

text.p: Libya on Wednesday signed with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) a cooperation agreement for studies of the rentability of its main chemical and petrochemical complexes, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported.
JANA, monitored in Tunis, said the agreement included 10 studies on the technical and economic rentability of the petrochemical Ras Lanuf and Abu Kammash chemical complexes.

The Ras Lanuf petrochemical complex, on the Gulf of Sirte, has the country's largest oil refinery built in 1985 with a planned capacity of 220,000 barrels per day, in addition to units such as an ethylene plant.
The Abu Kammash chemical complex, near the border with Tunisia, was opened in 1980. Among its products are acids, caustic sodas, liquid chlorine and salts.
JANA said the agreement was signed in Tripoli by UNDP representative Salah Bourgini and a senior official from the Libyan industry ministry.
